source_admission: Published values used as constants, quoted ranges or cited findings; no external dataset files are admitted. 'access' records how far each source was checked in this session: read here (the text or table was read), abstract (a summary or abstract was read), or not re-read here (a standard published value used from the literature, not checked against its source in this session). Model products of this repository are cited by path in the README and hashed in the results.

sources.citation: Quintiere 1989, Fire Safety Journal 15(1):3-29
sources.title: Scaling applications in fire research
sources.use: Froude scaling of fire: equal Q* = Q/(rho cp T sqrt(g) L^(5/2)), times as sqrt(L/g); the basis for carrying Earth correlations to lunar gravity
sources.access: not re-read here; the Froude-modelling approach is also described in Liao et al. (read here)

sources.citation: Heskestad, SFPE Handbook of Fire Protection Engineering, 'Fire Plumes, Flame Height, and Air Entrainment'
sources.title: Flame height L = D (15.6 N^(1/5) - 1.02) and its Earth form 0.235 Q^(2/5) - 1.02 D
sources.use: flame height with gravity, air density and the heat per kg of air
sources.access: not re-read here; standard published correlation

sources.citation: Huggett 1980, Fire and Materials 4(2):61-65
sources.title: Estimation of rate of heat release by means of oxygen consumption measurements
sources.use: 13.1 MJ released per kg of oxygen consumed
sources.access: not re-read here; standard published value

sources.citation: NFPA 92, Standard for Smoke Control Systems (2021), via Klote's AtriumCalc report for ASHRAE
sources.title: Axisymmetric plume and steady smoke-filling equations
sources.use: plume m = 0.071 Qc^(1/3) z^(5/3) + 0.0018 Qc above the flame, 0.032 Qc^(3/5) z within it, flame limit 0.166 Qc^(2/5); steady filling z/H = 1.11 - 0.28 ln(t Q^(1/3) H^(-4/3) / (A/H^2)) as a check
sources.access: plume equations read here in the AtriumCalc report; the filling equation from a search summary

sources.citation: Evans and Stroup 1985, NBSIR 85-3167
sources.title: Methods to calculate the response time of heat and smoke detectors installed below large unobstructed ceilings
sources.use: Heskestad and Delichatsios's t-squared ceiling-jet correlations (t2*, dT2*, u2*, A = g/(cp T rho); arrival 0.954(1 + r/H), dT2* = [(t2* - arrival)/(0.188 + 0.313 r/H)]^(4/3), u2*/sqrt(dT2*) = 0.59 (r/H)^-0.63) and the RTI response equation
sources.access: read here (equation set 2 and equation 1)

sources.citation: NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code, Annex B; NIST, 'Comments on correction factors for heat of combustion in NFPA 72 Appendix B'
sources.title: Detector response with the corrected Heskestad-Delichatsios constants
sources.use: the heat-of-combustion correction of 1.67 that turns the constants into 0.861, 0.146 and 0.242; the 13 K ceiling-jet rise as a surrogate for smoke detection
sources.access: the correction from a search summary of the NIST page; the resulting constants and the 13 K surrogate not re-read in NFPA 72 here

sources.citation: McCaffrey, Quintiere and Harkleroad 1981, Fire Technology 17(2):98-119
sources.title: Estimating room temperatures and the likelihood of flashover using fire test data correlations
sources.use: hot-layer rise 6.85 (Q^2/(Ao sqrt(Ho) hk AT))^(1/3), written with gravity explicit; flashover at a rise of about 500 K (610 (hk AT Ao sqrt(Ho))^(1/2) kW)
sources.access: not re-read here; standard published correlation

sources.citation: CEN 2002, EN 1991-1-2, Eurocode 1: Actions on structures, Part 1-2: Actions on structures exposed to fire, Annex E
sources.title: Fire load densities (Table E.4), fire growth rates and RHRf (Table E.5), ventilation-controlled heat release (E.6)
sources.use: design fires for each port use; t_alpha 600/300/150/75 s to 1 MW; ventilation-controlled 0.10 m Hu Av sqrt(heq) MW
sources.access: read here (Tables E.4 and E.5 and clause E.4)

sources.citation: Peatross and Beyler 1997, Fire Safety Science 5:403-414
sources.title: Ventilation effects on compartment fire characterization
sources.use: burning rate against oxygen, m/m0 = 10 X_O2 - 1.1 (0.65 at 17.46% relative to Earth's air)
sources.access: the correlation's form from search summaries of papers applying it; the original not re-read here

sources.citation: Ferkul and Olson 2011, Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer 25(3):457-461
sources.title: Zero-gravity centrifuge used for the evaluation of material flammability in lunar gravity
sources.use: Mylar G, Ultem 1000 and Nomex HT90-40 burned at lower oxygen in lunar gravity than in the 1 g upward test
sources.access: abstract summary; its numbers as tabled by Miller et al. (read here)

sources.citation: Olson et al. 2024, Fire Safety Journal
sources.title: Partial gravity flammability of cast PMMA rods in concurrent axial stagnation flow
sources.use: PMMA rods most flammable near lunar gravity (0.04 to 1 g, 13.2-15.2% O2)
sources.access: abstract, from a search summary

sources.citation: Feier, Shih, Sacksteder and T'ien 2002, Proceedings of the Combustion Institute 29:2569-2577
sources.title: Upward flame spread over thin solids in partial gravity
sources.use: upward flame spread over very thin fuels roughly proportional to gravity, as summarised by Liao et al.
sources.access: cited through Liao et al. (read here); the paper not read here

sources.citation: Liao, Carmignani, Niehaus and Gollner (with co-signers), decadal survey white paper
sources.title: Topical: Challenges and Research Needs for Micro- and Partial-Gravity Fires
sources.use: partial-gravity fire cannot be interpolated between 1 g and 0 g; partial-gravity tests limited to 20-30 s parabolic flights and the 5.18 s drop tower's centrifuge; lunar modules planned at 34% O2 and 56.5 kPa; Froude and pressure modelling
sources.access: read here

sources.title: FM2 experiment page

sources.access: read here

sources.citation: Linteris 2011, NIST final report to sponsor
sources.title: Large Scale Fire Dynamics in Spacecraft in Reduced Gravity
sources.use: FDS modified for variable gravity; at lunar or Martian gravity buoyant mixing keeps oxygen transport close to 1 g

sources.title: Pressure Flammability Thresholds of Selected Aerospace Materials
